implemented_requirements.requirement: Multiple strands of text are defined for each puzzle
implemented_requirements.evidence: puzzle.py – each Puzzle builds its strand_pool from the fragments of all Solution objects (see __post_init__ method). Example fragments: ["BUT", "TER", "FLY"] for the solution "BUTTERFLY".

implemented_requirements.requirement: Player can select and combine strands to form words/phrases
implemented_requirements.evidence: game.py – toggle_select() adds/removes strand indices from the current selection; submit() validates the selected fragments via MergeValidator.
validator.py – MergeValidator.validate() checks the concatenated, normalized selection against known target phrases, returning a MergeResult with status VALID, PARTIAL, ALREADY_FOUND or INVALID.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Feedback is given on merges (valid, partial, invalid, repeat)
implemented_requirements.evidence: ui.py – render_result() prints a tag ([VALID], [PARTIAL], etc.) and the validator's message; preview in render_selection() also shows a preview message.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Completion is detected when all strands are merged
implemented_requirements.evidence: game.py – is_complete() returns True when len(self.found) == len(self.solutions); main.py dispatches "complete" when a valid merge makes the game complete.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Command‑line interface for playing the puzzle
implemented_requirements.evidence: main.py – run_session() drives the game loop, parses commands via ui.parse_command, and calls dispatch() to handle select, submit, hint, etc.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Hint system that reveals a starting strand of an unfound merge
implemented_requirements.evidence: game.py – get_hint() picks a random remaining solution and marks its first strand as hinted.

critical_issues: Two UI modules exist (terminalui.py and ui.py); only ui.py is used, so terminalui.py is dead code but does not affect execution.
No explicit __main__ guard in ui.py, but main.py provides the entry point, so this is harmless.
judge.summary: The repository contains a complete, runnable implementation of a "Strands" word‑segmentation puzzle. Puzzles are defined with multiple strand fragments, the game engine lets the player select strands, validates merges, provides real‑time feedback, offers hints, and correctly detects when all merges are found. Minor code duplication (unused terminalui.py) does not impede functionality, and the overall design meets the benchmark requirements.
